name: Duskframe Crowd-Walker Operative Set
description: A deceptively ordinary-looking ensemble built for runners who need to vanish into Tier 2-3 foot traffic. The centerpiece is a reversible field jacket in dusty slate on one side and oil-stained rust-brown on the other — both sides treated with scatter-weave scanner-resistant fiber panels sewn into the lining, making it opaque to standard port and transit body scanners. The jacket's interior is a maze of flat holster channels, zippered tool sleeves, and a reinforced spine channel that routes aug-power cabling from a hip-mount battery pack to shoulder-level chrome. Collar is slightly raised, hiding a folded balaclava that deploys in seconds. Underneath sits a dark teal compression shirt with embedded comm-wire loops at the collar and reinforced left-side panels where a subdermal rig typically presses. Bottoms are a pair of deep charcoal straight-leg trousers with double-layer knee panels and two concealed thigh-pockets sewn flush against the inseam — invisible when standing, accessible with one hand. Footwear is a low-profile slate-grey street boot with silent-tread soles and a magnetic ankle clip that releases a folded ankle holster. A worn canvas tote bag completes the look — utterly forgettable, internally lined with signal-dampening mesh.
functionality: Reversible jacket for quick identity shift, scanner-resistant panels in jacket and bag, interior holster channels and tool sleeves, aug-power routing spine channel, comm-wire loops at collar, concealed thigh and ankle holsters, silent-tread soles
what_it_says: This is someone who has spent years perfecting the art of looking unremarkable. The wear patterns are calculated — scuffs where a transit worker would have them, the tote bag that reads as a lunch haul. Anyone who knows the trade recognizes the jacket's slightly stiff shoulders for what they are. Everyone else sees a shift worker heading home.
worn_by: mid-tier runners who specialize in social infiltration
couriers moving sensitive packages through checkpoints
fixers who need to move between neighborhoods without burning their cover
manufacturer: Ashgrain Collective — street label, Circuit District, unlicensed
story_hooks: A runner in this outfit is stopped at a Kelvex transit checkpoint — the scanner clears them, but a sharp-eyed platform officer notices the jacket's collar is slightly too stiff and the tote bag sits oddly flat. Does the runner talk their way through or burn the exit route?

The rust-brown side of the jacket was last worn during a job that went badly. Someone in the right circles recognizes the specific patchwork repair on the left sleeve — and that person shouldn't be alive.

A client insists on a meeting in a Tier 3 corporate atrium where the dress code is enforced by facial-recognition doors. The charcoal trousers pass, but the jacket's scanner resistance trips an anomaly flag in the building's security AI.
